metadata.methods_description: Each session comprised 50 trials (2 practice, 48 experimental). Each trial had two learning trials, in which participants were driven to a visible object, followed by one test trial, in which they navigated from a random start location and orientation to the remembered location of the invisible object. Trials were counterbalanced using reflected object and start positions. iEEG was recorded with Blackrock or Medtronic systems and provided in both monopolar and bipolar montages, with MNI and Talairach coordinates when available.

citation_details.title: Brain state sets the spatial scale at which cortical geometry constrains human cortical dynamics
citation_details.author: Alejandro Salinas-Medina, Anisleidy González Mitjans, P.-J. Toussaint, Xue Liu, Alan Charles Evans

citation_details.title: Spatial Memory of Object Locations with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
citation_details.author: Haydn G. Herrema, Michael J. Kahana
citation_details.abstract: This dataset contains intracranial electrophysiological recordings and behavioral data from a spatial navigation memory task with open-loop brain stimulation during encoding. Participants learned object locations through guided navigation and subsequently recalled them during self-navigation test phases. The study employed electrical stimulation of hippocampal and entorhinal cortex electrodes during learning trials, with stimulation parameters systematically varied across counterbalanced trial blocks to investigate the effects of targeted brain stimulation on spatial memory encoding. This dataset is an open-loop stimulation variant of the YC1 dataset (ds005522).
